title: How the umbilical cord forms

objective.text: Trace how the umbilical cord forms, from the umbilical ring to birth.

body.general: How does a baby end up joined to the placenta by one cord? In week 5, stalks leave the embryo through the umbilical ring [f1]. One, the connecting stalk, carries a pouch, the allantois, plus two arteries and a vein [f2]. Another, the yolk stalk or vitelline duct, leads to the yolk sac [f3]. The amnion, the fluid-filled sac, wraps them into one cord [f5]. From week 6 gut loops sit in the cord, returning by about week 12 after fertilization [f7]. By birth only two arteries and a vein remain, in protective Wharton jelly [f8,f9].
body.mbbs: In week 5 the primitive umbilical ring, the amnion–ectoderm junction, transmits three structures [f1]. The connecting stalk carries the allantois, two umbilical arteries and one vein [f2]. The yolk stalk (vitelline duct) carries the vitelline vessels [f3]. A canal links the intraembryonic and extraembryonic cavities [f4]. The expanding amnion wraps these into the primitive umbilical cord [f5]. From week 6 gut loops lie in the cord as a physiological hernia, returning by about week 12 after fertilization [f7]. At the end of month 3 the amnion meets the chorion, obliterating the chorionic cavity [f6]. As the allantois and vitelline structures regress, two arteries and one vein remain in Wharton jelly [f8]. The jelly is proteoglycan-rich and protective [f9]. The arteries' muscular, elastic walls contract quickly after the cord is tied [f10]. At term the cord is 1–2 cm thick and 50–60 cm long [f11]. Insertion is usually eccentric, sometimes marginal, rarely velamentous [f13].

facts.text: In week 5, structures pass through the primitive umbilical ring, where the amnion meets the embryo's ectoderm.
The connecting stalk passes through the ring, carrying the allantois, two umbilical arteries and one umbilical vein.
The yolk stalk (vitelline duct) and its vessels also pass through the ring.
So does a canal that joins the cavities inside and outside the embryo.
As the amnion expands, it wraps the stalks together into the primitive umbilical cord.
At the end of month 3 the amnion reaches the chorion and the chorionic cavity closes.
From week 6, gut loops lie in the cord as a normal physiological hernia; they return by about week 12 after fertilization.
Once the allantois, vitelline duct and vitelline vessels are gone, the cord holds two arteries and one vein in Wharton jelly.
Wharton jelly is rich in proteoglycans and protects the cord vessels.
The umbilical arteries have muscular, elastic walls that clamp down quickly after the cord is tied.
At birth the cord is about 1–2 cm thick and 50–60 cm long, often twisted, with false knots.
Cord length reflects how much the fetus moves.
The cord usually joins the placenta off-centre, sometimes at its edge, and rarely into the membranes outside it (velamentous insertion).
About 1 in 200 newborns have only one umbilical artery.
The book reports heart or other blood-vessel defects in about 20 % of babies with a single umbilical artery.
The umbilical arteries carry the fetus's used blood to the placenta; the umbilical vein brings oxygen-rich blood back.
facts.note: dossier §6 m5: Ch 13 fetal circulation; Ch 8 gives no flow direction

facts.text: Beyond Langman: a single umbilical artery found on its own carries no extra risk of chromosome disorders.

misconceptions.wrong: Umbilical arteries carry oxygen-rich blood because they are arteries.
misconceptions.right: They carry the fetus's used blood to the placenta; the single vein brings oxygen-rich blood back.

misconceptions.wrong: Gut in the cord at 9 weeks means an omphalocele.
misconceptions.right: It is normal: gut loops sit in the cord from week 6 and return by about week 12 after fertilization.

checks.prompt: Put the steps in forming the umbilical cord in order.
options: Stalks pass through the primitive umbilical ring
The amnion wraps the stalks into the primitive cord
The amnion reaches the chorion and the chorionic cavity closes
checks.why: The stalks pass the ring in week 5, the amnion then wraps them, and by the end of month 3 it reaches the chorion.

checks.prompt: What does the umbilical cord hold at birth?
options: Two arteries and one vein in Wharton jelly
One artery and two veins in Wharton jelly
Two arteries, one vein and the open allantois
One artery and one vein in Wharton jelly
checks.why: The allantois and vitelline structures are gone by then, leaving two arteries and one vein in jelly.

checks.prompt: At 9 weeks after fertilization, loops of gut are seen in the cord. What is this most likely to be?
options: A normal stage: gut loops sit in the cord for a while
checks.why: Gut loops normally sit in the cord from week 6 and return by about week 12 after fertilization.

clinical: About 1 in 200 newborns have only one umbilical artery [f14]. In the book's figures, about 20 % of these babies also have heart or other blood-vessel defects [f15].

remember.q: What does the umbilical cord hold at birth?
remember.a: Two arteries and one vein in Wharton jelly [f8].

remember.q: Which structure wraps the stalks into the cord?
Which way do the umbilical arteries carry blood?
remember.a: From the fetus to the placenta, carrying used blood [f16].
